organism: Xanthobacter sp. SoF1 (Solar Foods); Cupriavidus necator in other programmes
feedstock: Electrolytic H2 and O2; CO2 from direct air capture or point source; ammonia; minerals
trl_2026: 7 (demonstration plant operating; first commercial plant planned)
leading_actors: Solar Foods (Finland) with GEA, Fortum; Ajinomoto as food partner; Air Protein and Kiverdi (US) status not verified
largest_plant_capacity_t_per_yr: Scaling to 230 (Factory 01, Finland); Factory 02 phase one 3,200, targeted late 2028 (decision intended during 2026)
approvals: Singapore novel food 29 Sep 2022; US self-affirmed GRAS, FDA notice filed May 2026, pending; EU EFSA opinion pending (Sep 2026)
energy_kwh_per_kg_protein: 69 to 83 (2030 design, incl. DAC and on-site NH3); 61 to 70 (2050 design)
cost_2026_usd_per_kg_protein: 6.6 to 7.3 (modelled FOAK at best global sites, 2028); real FOAK likely higher
cost_2030: 4.8 to 5.4 best global sites; Vietnam 6.9 to 12.6 (our estimate)
cost_2040: Vietnam 4.7 to 8.6 (our estimate); best sites 3.7 to 4.2 in 2035
cost_2050: 2.5 to 2.8 best global sites; Vietnam 3.3 to 6.5 (our estimate)
vn_window_conditions: Delivered green H2 at or below about USD 1.5 to 2 per kg at high utilisation (bulk feed; food-grade protein can bear a higher price); firmed renewable power at or below about USD 30 to 45 per MWh; WACC at or below about 8%; point-source CO2 at USD 20 to 50 per t; a novel-food route (food) or a feed-list entry for bacterial biomass (feed); fishmeal protein above about USD 3,000 per t or a carbon price on competing proteins
signposts: Solar Foods FID (2026) and Factory 02 start (late 2028); EFSA opinion and FDA letter; Vietnamese green H2 plant completion (Vinh Long); Vietnamese LCOH quotes below USD 2 per kg; legal track for offshore wind for new energy
source_ids: FTG-01; FTG-03; FTG-04; FTG-05; FTG-18; FTG-19
evidence_label: general (technology); VN-direct inputs for Vietnam estimates
confidence: Medium (published model and company data); Low for Vietnam estimates
notes: Best-site costs are Fasihi et al. 2025 (7% WACC, EUR x 1.2 = USD). Vietnam estimates: electricity use x Vietnamese supply price (BNEF solar LCOE x 1.4 to 1.54 balancing) + Fasihi non-energy costs x 1.15 to 1.35 for WACC 9 to 11%; see ftg_estimates.py. Solar Foods Factory 02 plan (EUR 191 M on balance sheet for 3,200 t) implies about EUR 60,000 per annual t of product, far above the TEA capex (our derivation, Low).

route: Hydrogen-oxidising bacteria, feed grade (techno-economic studies only)
organism: Cupriavidus necator and mixed hydrogen-oxidising cultures
feedstock: H2 from wind or solar electrolysis; point-source CO2 (e.g. ethanol plant) or DAC
leading_actors: Academic TEAs (Iowa State; Weizmann and partners); NovoNutrients closed 2025; no feed plant found
energy_kwh_per_kg_protein: About 69 to 83 (same physics as food grade; less downstream processing)
h2_kg_per_kg_protein: 0.69 (Fasihi stoichiometry); 0.43 to 0.56 kg per kg biomass in other TEAs
cost_2026_usd_per_kg_protein: About 3.2 (Jean and Brown 2024 MSP USD 2,070 per t SCP at 65% protein, electricity USD 11.4 per MWh); 4 to 5 (Leger et al. 2021)
cost_2030: Not separately projected; see food-grade row
vn_window_conditions: As food grade, plus a feed-list entry for bacterial biomass (MAE) and a fishmeal-protein price well above 2025 levels
signposts: Any feed-grade hydrogen-oxidiser plant above 1,000 t per year anywhere; MAE listing of bacterial SCP
notes: Fasihi et al. judge the Jean and Brown power price 'unrealistically low without subsidies'. Leger et al.: cost above fishmeal (about USD 2.5 per kg protein) and soybean meal (about USD 1) at the time.

route: Methanotroph single-cell protein on natural gas
feedstock: Natural gas (methane), oxygen or air, ammonia
leading_actors: Calysta and Calysseo (Adisseo JV, China); Unibio (Denmark) with SIIG (Saudi Arabia); String Bio (India, not verified)
largest_plant_capacity_t_per_yr: 20,000 nameplate (Calysseo, Chongqing, company website FM-13; FTG-06 calls it demonstration-scale; halted 2026); 50,000 planned (Unibio and SIIG, Saudi Arabia, commercial 2028)
approvals: EU feed (natural-gas bacterial protein since the 1990s; UniProtein); China MARA full approval 2024 (FeedKind, aquafeed); Saudi aquaculture (Unibio); EU pet food (Unibio); China pet food expected Q3 2026 (FeedKind)
energy_kwh_per_kg_protein: About 26 (methane energy, HHV, at 1.7 kg CH4 per kg protein); process electricity not found
cost_2026_usd_per_kg_protein: 1.10 to 2.57 (one TEA, cited); real operations loss-making (Calysseo 2025 revenue USD 0.71 M, net loss USD 15.5 M)
vn_window_conditions: Methane below about USD 5 per MMBtu (stranded gas or aggregated biogas); a feed-list entry for methanotroph meal; buyers paying a functional premium in shrimp feed
signposts: Calysseo refinancing and restart; Unibio Saudi plant start (2028); Vietnamese industrial gas price path; FeedKind or UniProtein trials in Vietnamese shrimp feed
notes: Our estimate: gas alone costs USD 0.72 to 1.25 per kg protein at USD 8 to 14 per MMBtu (1.7 kg CH4 per kg protein x 0.0526 MMBtu per kg), close to the whole price of soybean-meal protein (about USD 0.88). Earlier gas-based protein proved uneconomic because of the high price of natural gas (Kuzniar et al. 2019). Fossil methane gives no carbon benefit.

feedstock: Biogas (about 50 to 65% CH4) from cassava-starch wastewater, pig manure, landfill
leading_actors: University groups (India, China, Denmark, Australia); Vietnam: one 2016 methanotroph isolation for SCP (VNU Hanoi)
vn_window_conditions: Aggregated biogas from starch factories or large pig farms at one site; low-cost gas cleaning; a feed-list entry
signposts: A pilot at a Tay Ninh or Dong Nai starch factory; national biogas inventory
notes: Version 0.1 found cassava-starch wastewater biogas widespread but unquantified. Plants are small and dispersed, which works against the scale economies of gas fermentation.

feedstock: Steel-mill and ferroalloy off-gas (CO, CO2, H2); protein is a co-product of ethanol
leading_actors: Beijing Shougang LanzaTech (plants in Hebei, Ningxia, Guizhou); CAAS Feed Research Institute; LanzaTech (licensor)
largest_plant_capacity_t_per_yr: 5,000 protein (Hebei plant, with 45,000 ethanol); group protein output 10,200 in 2023
approvals: China MARA new feed raw material certificate 29 Aug 2021
energy_kwh_per_kg_protein: Not reported (energy comes from the off-gas)
cost_2026_usd_per_kg_protein: Not published; company gross margin negative in H1 2024; priced against imported fishmeal
vn_window_conditions: A Vietnamese steel or ferroalloy site with surplus off-gas not already used for power, and a gas-to-ethanol or SAF business case; a feed-list entry for CAP
signposts: Hoa Phat or Formosa Ha Tinh announcing gas fermentation or SAF; CAP imports into Vietnam; MAE listing
notes: Protein is only 0.1 to 0.15 t per t ethanol. Group protein output was 10,200 t in 2023. Hoa Phat already burns its off-gases for 80 to 90% power self-sufficiency, so the gas is not free.

route: Two-stage off-gas or CO2 to acetate, then aerobic single-cell protein
organism: Acetogens, then yeast or bacteria (e.g. Yarrowia lipolytica, Cupriavidus)
feedstock: Industrial off-gas or CO2 plus H2
leading_actors: Bio Base Europe Pilot Plant and Ghent University (TEA); Chinese academic groups
cost_2026_usd_per_kg_protein: About 5.9 (USD 4.15 per kg SCP at an assumed 70% protein; 2.78 per kg SCP if intensified, about 4.0 per kg protein)
vn_window_conditions: As for CAP, plus low-cost H2 if the gas is CO2-rich
signposts: A pilot above 1 t per day
notes: Vlaeminck et al. 2023: 20,000 t per year feed SCP, USD 320 M capex; facility-dependent costs 58%, utilities 18%. The 70% protein content is our assumption.

organism: Pichia pastoris (Komagataella phaffii) in China; historically Methylophilus methylotrophus (ICI Pruteen)
feedstock: Methanol (coal-based today; e-methanol from CO2 and H2 possible later)
trl_2026: 7 to 8 in China (10,000 t class demonstration referred to, not verified)
leading_actors: Tianjin Institute of Industrial Biotechnology (CAS) and partners
approvals: None found this round (MARA lists not fully searched)
energy_kwh_per_kg_protein: For e-methanol: electrosynthesis efficiency 50 to 60% vs 65 to 75% for H2 (Leger et al. 2021)
cost_2026_usd_per_kg_protein: About 4 to 5 (Leger et al. 2021 for PV-methanol SCP, USD 2.8 per kg dry biomass)
vn_window_conditions: Cheap low-carbon methanol (e.g. a Dung Quat e-methanol project); methanol logistics are easier than H2
signposts: A Chinese new-feed certificate for methanol protein; BSR low-carbon methanol pilot at Dung Quat
notes: TIB reports 67.2% crude protein and 92% of theoretical methanol-to-protein conversion (Jan 2024). Methanol from coal carries a high carbon footprint.

vn_window_conditions: Not favourable: Vietnam imported 81,500 of 103,700 m3 of ethanol supplied in July 2026 for E10 (v0.1), so ethanol is not a cheap local feedstock
signposts: Domestic ethanol surplus after E10 demand
notes: Gap: route not researched in depth this round.

route: Electro-microbial protein (CO2 electrolysis to acetate or formate, then microbes)
organism: Yeasts, algae or bacteria growing on electro-acetate or formate
leading_actors: Tianjin Institute of Industrial Biotechnology; Xi'an Jiaotong University; US academic groups
energy_kwh_per_kg_protein: Higher than the H2 route (formate electrosynthesis efficiency 30 to 50%)
cost_2026_usd_per_kg_protein: Not established; formate route 'considerably more expensive' than H2 (Leger et al. 2021)
vn_window_conditions: Only after about 2035 if CO2 electrolysers mature; no Vietnamese capability found
signposts: Any pilot above 1 t per day; electrolyser efficiency above 60% for acetate
notes: China leads publications on this route.

feedstock: Sunlight, CO2 (flue gas or purified), nutrients
trl_2026: 9 on purchased CO2 (spirulina); 6 to 7 on flue gas
leading_actors: Many global producers; small Vietnamese spirulina producers
approvals: Spirulina is an ordinary food; algae are on Vietnam's feed list (v0.1)
vn_window_conditions: Near-pure CO2 from ethanol or brewing; land near CO2 sources; a buyer for high-value biomass
signposts: A Vietnamese spirulina or chlorella plant using captured CO2
notes: Janssen et al. 2022 give a potential of 22 to 44 t protein per ha per year in closed systems, similar to or above PV-driven SCP (about 13 to 22 t per ha in Vietnam, our estimate). Version 0.1 rates microalgae a niche with incumbents.
